Prior: 21896 at 2026-08-11 (v0.24.0: +2354, the largest single increment in this project's history and the one that most needed the ratchet to force an argument for it. W7a is a feature that WRITES TO THE OPERATOR'S ~/.claude/settings.json, so the code that is not the feature is the code that keeps it from doing damage, and that is most of the line count. Roughly: ~600 for internal/orch/hostcfg (an order-preserving JSON editor; the obvious map[string]any implementation alphabetises every key and re-indents every nested value, which on a hand-maintained git-tracked settings.json is an unreadable whole-file diff on every install, so it was never a viable option), ~1050 for the install/uninstall state machine across three files (plan, read-only assess, apply with rollback, reverse), and the REMAINING ~700 is the adversarial-review round -- three fresh-context specialists, every finding reproduced against running code, every one ending in a damaged or unrecoverable operator config. Those seven: (1) any `claude` invocation, even a read-only `mcp list`, REWRITES settings.json (normalises `model`, re-indents), so hashing the bytes we wrote recorded a hash stale before install returned and the byte-identical restore path would have been dead code on every real machine -- hashes now come from disk after all steps; (2) a SECOND install overwrote the pre-install backup with already-installed bytes while the manifest kept install #1's hash, so the integrity check could never match again and uninstall hard-failed permanently with the config still wired; (3) an unparseable entry OF OURS read as 'already gone', so uninstall reported ok, deleted the manifest, and left the hook wired with nothing on disk claiming ownership -- absence must be PROVED, so the lookup gained a third answer, the same absent-vs-undetermined trichotomy Presence already carries for files; (4) a statusLine that was present but whose command could not be read (a `static` type, or the bare-string form) got the tee wired over it with an empty delegate, rendering a BLANK status bar from a run that reported success; (5) -home isolated only the host config, so a scratch install wrote its manifest, backups, tee and delegate into the operator's REAL ~/.meta-router, planting an ownership claim that then made the real install refuse permanently; (6) rollback ran forward, deleting the tee script before restoring the settings.json that referenced it, and reported failures only to stderr where they died with the scrollback; (7) the registry undo ran unprobed, so a server the operator had already removed made `claude mcp remove` exit 1 and abort the whole uninstall with everything still wired, on every retry. Also in that round: manifest steps are validated per kind before being acted on (an empty Ident made `strings.Contains(x, "")` true, so ANY operator statusLine read as ours and the restore wrote an absent Prior into the file), MemberSet/ArrayAppend refuse non-JSON (reindent fell back to its input on error, so an invalid value was stored, rendered and saved with a nil error -- the very corruption the package exists to prevent, arriving through the package itself), duplicate keys are refused rather than collapsed last-wins, CRLF/BOM/key-spelling/blank-line-indent are all preserved, and array entries are re-located by ident at removal time rather than by an index that goes stale after the first removal. The honest summary: the feature is ~1650 lines and the evidence that it is safe is ~700, and both numbers are the cost of a command whose failure mode is an operator's config).
